key_insight: A deep neural operator can learn the mapping from initial/boundary conditions to both the solution and evolving free boundary, delivering high-precision, fast predictions for free boundary PDEs such as tumour growth.
problem_solved: Traditional numerical solvers for free boundary problems are accurate but computationally expensive and slow for patient-specific or real-time use; this method enables fast, accurate simulation of moving interfaces.
method: Train a deep neural operator to approximate the solution operator for PDEs with moving/free boundaries, learning from solution trajectories rather than per-instance meshes.
Represent the free boundary as an evolving interface (differentiable or level-set style) and predict its dynamics jointly with field variables.
Incorporate physics constraints and data-driven examples to improve accuracy and generalization for a range of initial/boundary conditions.
impact: Enables real-time, high-fidelity simulation of free-boundary phenomena (e.g., tumour growth), making operator-based surrogate models viable for clinical decision support and rapid what-if studies in ML-for-physics applications.
visual_elements: Schematic: operator block mapping input conditions to solution field + evolving interface
Sequence animation: time-lapse of predicted free-boundary (tumour) growth vs ground truth
Bar/line chart: accuracy and runtime comparison against traditional solvers
Icon set: "real-time" stopwatch, medical cross for clinical relevance, equation/PDE symbol for physics
paper_title: Deep neural operator for free boundary problems
paper_authors: Zongjia Long, Qi Zhou, Aiqing Zhu, Dong Dai, Yiqun Liu
